interpretation.diagram_classification: Theological / exegetical diagram: concentric schematic plan with gates, probably an allegorical plan of a sacred dwelling or city.
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram seems to be an allegorical scheme of a sacred enclosure. The central circle reads "Habitacio Legis 7 Sacerdotuus". The "7" is probably the Tironian sign for "et", so the text would read roughly 'dwelling of the Law and of the priesthood'. This marks the centre as the most sacred zone. The surrounding inner ring carries further words, each starting with "Habitacio" or a similar word, possibly 'dwelling of the prophets' ("Prophara" may be "Prophetarum"). This suggests a hierarchy of groups, such as the Law, priests and prophets, arranged around the centre. The outer ring is interrupted by rectangular compartments set at intervals around it. One reads "Dera stru quilinii", which may be 'porta aquilonis' (north gate), and another begins "Pozca"/"Porta". They look like labelled gates or entrances, probably naming directions or the tribes or peoples associated with them. Taken together, the diagram probably presents a Temple, tabernacle or city-like structure in which the central Law and priesthood are surrounded by other groups and entered through gates. The exact source and the meaning of each sector remain uncertain.
interpretation.evidence: The reading of the central text "Habitacio Legis 7 Sacerdotuus" is fairly clear and supports the 'dwelling' interpretation. The ring words ("Habitacio", "Prophara", "Modesti [illegible]", "Siui", "Z") are only partly legible. The gate reading depends on the uncertain transcription "Dera stru quilinii", and several compartments are illegible. The concentric layout with compartments breaking the outer ring visually suggests a plan with gates. No source can be named with confidence. In Step 1 the rectangular compartments were typed "figurative", although they are geometric or text-bearing shapes. The Step 1 readings "Sacerdotuus", "Modesti" and "Siui" are tentative. The "Z" sign may be another abbreviation sign. The number of compartments (six recorded) may be incomplete, since the left side of the diagram is partly cut off.

interpretation.interpretation: The concentric structure expresses a gradation from the sacred centre outwards. The innermost circle holds the Law and the priesthood, the middle ring holds other groups or functions, and the outer ring holds the thresholds or gates. This implies that access to the centre passes through the outer zones and the gates.
interpretation.evidence: Step 1 entries 1 and 2 record the nested rings, and the central circle has a distinct dotted border. The outer compartments cross the outer ring band. Different ink colours separate the zones: black for the centre and gate texts, orange-red for the ring words.
